prerequisites: Second study section reached (at least 42 ECTS credits from the first study section must be proven).
Proficiency in C programming language, especially records, multidimensional arrays, pointers.
Proficiency in Java programming language, especially threads.

learning_outcomes.text: Students are able to apply their knowledge of fundamental paradigms for distributed systems in practice.
Students are able to use their knowledge of fundamental problems in the field of distributed systems and especially parallel programming and their elimination.
Students are able to practically apply language features of the C and JAVA programming languages to describe distributed systems.
Students are able to use their knowledge of specification languages (e.g., UML, process calculi) and to describe distributed systems both abstractly and with concrete examples.
Students are able to apply their knowledge of analysis and design of distributed systems to specific problems.
Students are able to solve the problem of mutual exclusion in the context of known standard applications (barrier synchronization, Read/Writer, Consumer/Producer) in C and Java.

syllabus_topics: Language features for describing parallel and communicating programs
Problems in Distributed Systems (Safety, Security, Voting procedures, ...)
Synchronization of Distributed Systems in C and Java
assessment_rules: Successful completion of the practical course (15.2) is a prerequisite for participation in the lecture (15.1). The successful completion of 5 exercise sheets is required as proof of performance. This will check the ability to solve practical problems in distributed systems, the use of semaphores and monitors, and the use of C and Java for problems in parallel programming and distributed systems.
